# Code of conduct

This project is run by one person as a personal documentation kit, shared publicly under CC BY 4.0. The bar for participation is low (be a reasonable adult), but it's worth being explicit about what that means.

## Where this applies

Anywhere related to this project: issues, pull requests, discussions, and any direct communication about the work.

## What's expected

- Stay focused on the content: is it accurate, is it useful, is it correctly scoped.
- Argue about the documents, not the person who wrote them.
- Assume good faith until there's evidence otherwise.
- If you make a mistake, fix it. A short apology is enough.

## What's not acceptable

- Personal attacks, harassment, or hostility.
- Discriminatory language or behaviour on any basis.
- Trolling, brigading, or deliberately wasting other people's time.
- Publishing someone's private information without permission.

If a reasonable person would think something else is out of bounds, treat it as out of bounds too.

## Reporting

If someone's behaviour towards you on this project crosses a line, email security@infosek.com.au. Reports are confidential.

This is a one-maintainer project. If the issue is with the maintainer, you have a few options: raise it in the relevant issue or PR, escalate to [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/), or step away.

## What happens after a report

I'll acknowledge the report within a reasonable timeframe and look into it. Responses might include a private conversation with the person reported, a public note in the relevant thread, locking or hiding comments, or blocking the person from the repository. I'll communicate the outcome to whoever reported the issue.

## Scope and inspiration

Draws on the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), deliberately shorter and more direct: written for a project this size, not a large community.
